ratings_why.fun: Every fight has a payoff moment when a death knocks and a spider stabs out, and the open-or-wait choice each turn is real; the board is mostly closed doors until the fight starts.
ratings_why.distinct: 8 because the board you show is not the board you fight with: untargetable Lids, scouting that shows only doors, and a front row of Lids that sends attacks into your back row. No tribe today or in a generic auto-battler does that.

verdict_why: The idea is settled and reads well, but The Past Master and the Sexton need their rules made plain before a player can read them.

points.text: The Past Master says "Your Spring effects trigger twice" but the builds treat it as Spring text only. Say whether the Spring attack also happens twice.

The Under-Chamber Sexton adds a second unit per slot with no rules for it: can the unit above be a Lid, what scouting shows, and what happens when a summon wants that slot. One line on what stacking means would make it readable.
Patient's "Lids can only stay shut if you won" reads like a separate rule. Say it as the result: if you lose, every Lid ends up open, so only a win makes units Patient.
Take the designer's own option and show each closed door's Knock when scouting. A door marked with its knock is still a secret, but a player can plan around it.
Signora Corkhinge's "each other friendly unit that Springs first gains +4/+4" trips the eye; "Before another friendly unit Springs, it gains +4/+4" reads at a glance.

standouts.why: Grit-Lid Purseweb is the whole tribe in five words: the enemy across attacks, and the spider stabs it back.
Slit-Mender Purseweb strikes, mends its lid and waits again, so one enemy keeps getting stabbed. It plays exactly like the real spider.
Brother Pardo Ashby springs out with two Nieces on his back, and the Nieces are bait for the next Lid. Clear, funny and useful.

weakest.why: Ballot Clerk is a plain gold piece; the ballot box theme never shows up in what it does.
Under-Chamber Sexton is the hardest card to read, with a new stacking rule and a two-part Knock on one card.
Usher of the Degrees is a strong idea in a long sentence, with a Knock inside its When played text that is easy to misread.

flags.note: Does "Spring effects" include the Spring attack?
Two units in one slot has no stated rules.
With The Past Master and Corkhinge, the replayed cascade could be very large and hard to follow on screen.
Mabyn squares the Patient count and stacks with Old Diadem; shut Lids also count for hero damage.
